title: Prefix-LM: bidirectional attention over the theorem statement (up to the prompt's first `by`), causal over the proof, with encoder-ALiBi (2x slope to the right) inside the prefix, on the 115-fable hybrid ALiBi/NoPE Lean incumbent (4.80M params)
description: New mechanism, not in the P01-P50 backlog (closest: positional/attention family P32-P34, T5/prefix-LM literature). The theorem statement tokens (left-padded prompt through its first `by`) attend to each other in every block in both directions, so each premise's representation can condition on the goal and the other premises before the first proof token is generated; proof tokens stay causal, the loss stays on proof tokens only, and the prefix flag is derived from idx alone so the frozen loss_on, RL fine-tune and generate (prompt prefill then one-token steps with the cached bidirectional prompt K/V) all see the same function. Expected to help expert iteration because premise selection for 7+ line proofs needs goal-conditioned premise encodings that a causal prefix cannot build.
hypothesis: Under causal attention, the token at premise h_k cannot see the goal C or later premises, so the proof-relevant computation ('which premises matter for this goal') can only happen at the last few prompt positions and then be re-derived by every proof token through attention. A bidirectional prefix lets the six blocks build goal-conditioned premise representations once, in the prompt, which the causal proof then reads; that is the encoder-decoder inductive bias that T5/prefix-LM pretraining found best for conditional generation. Expert iteration on 7+ line targets, whose prompts have more premises and deeper goals than the cap-6 pretraining data, should benefit most. Risks: NoPE heads get no positional signal at all inside the prefix (only content and the 4 ALiBi heads carry order), and the (B,H,T,T) mask costs some throughput (steps -3 to -8%).
expected_delta: -40 to +60 dev solves >= 7 vs 115-fable's 631 (central +15); pretraining steps 3,900-4,300 (115: ~4,200), final val loss 0.079-0.086; round-1 targets solved within +-100 of 115's; totals 1,400-1,800 s under the 2,400 s cap

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) with Peri-LN blocks and hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads as in 115-fable; CHANGED: prefix-LM attention mask (bidirectional within the theorem statement, causal elsewhere)
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope as in 115 (slopes 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256, 0, 0, 0, 0), bias -slope_h * dist where CHANGED dist = (q - k) for keys at or before the query and 2 * (k - q) for prefix keys to the right of the query (Press's encoder-ALiBi asymmetric slopes: locality kept, direction preserved); -inf where not allowed
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: CHANGED vs 115-fable: ALiBiGPT.forward computes prefix = tokens up to and including the row's first `by` token (tok.stoi['by']), excluding pad, from idx; allowed = (causal, or the harness mask when given) OR (query in prefix AND key in prefix); the prefix flag of every key is stored in caches[0]['prefix'] next to the key positions so cached decoding matches the full forward; dist for right-hand prefix keys is 2 * distance; bias built with torch.where so the training bias is (B,H,T,T) instead of (1,H,T,T). Constructor takes by_id and pad_id. PeriLNBlock, width, heads, depth, GELU, untied embedding/readout, ln_f, init, optimizer and schedule are byte-identical to 115.
arch.n_params_detail: identical to 115-fable: 4,800,000 (vocab 107); no new parameters, the prefix flag is derived from tokens
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 256, 8, by_id=tok.stoi['by'], pad_id=0) from this pretrain.py, blocks replaced by PeriLNBlock, then load state (same keys as 115). Loading these weights into 115's causal model gives a different function (the prompt K/V differ).
arch.kv_cache: caches[0] holds key positions and CHANGED key prefix flags; the prompt prefill (sample.generate: whole left-padded prompt in one forward with causal+keep mask) is where the bidirectional prompt K/V are computed and cached; later one-token proof steps are proof tokens (prefix False) so they use the harness mask unchanged. No local CPU equivalence check was run this session (time cap); the mask logic mirrors 115's cached-position handling.

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: CHANGED: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2 (070-claude: 1), head (99,256) 1. Every Muon update now has element RMS ~1/16 times lr; only fc2's step doubles.
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: unchanged from 101-claude: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: CHANGED: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: CHANGED: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, CHANGED: + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW
optimizer.parameters: unchanged from 101-claude: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)

config.init: Fork default construction (normal 0.02 embedding/readout), blocks replaced by PeriLNBlocks and re-initialized with the fork _init (zero biases), then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); output LayerNorms gain 1, bias 0 (standard Peri-LN / OLMo 2 / Gemma 2 init). RNG draws shift vs 101-claude because the blocks are built twice. At init each branch write has RMS ~1 instead of ~0.1
